audit_findings.title: Post-year-end acquisition is missing from the valuation perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.0m final purchase consideration, comprising $12.974m cash paid less $4.746m cash acquired for $8.228m net cash paid; $13.0m is 6.2% of the $210m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The June 2026 cash bridge reflects the acquisition payment, but the operating forecast and FY2025 OE anchor exclude Interworks earnings and reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 24, 2026, the Company entered into a Share Purchase Agreement (the “Interworks Purchase Agreement”) and purchased one hundred percent of the issued and outstanding share capital of Interworks Single Member SA (“Interworks”), a Greek société anonyme, from Infiterra Holding Limited, a company incorporated in Cyprus, for an aggregate purchase price of approximately €8.0 million (subject to certain adjustments).
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, not hypothetical. Interworks was acquired before the valuation date and is consolidated in the June balance sheet, yet the valuation perimeter is null. The acquired operation contributed $0.2m of net income and $1.4m of gross profit from acquisition through June 2026. Charging the cash payment without including the acquired operating claim tends to understate value, and the purchase-price scale is material relative to the base valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rerun using a June 2026 perimeter that includes Interworks normalized OE and reinvestment, including acquired liabilities and purchase-price-allocation effects; alternatively reverse every Interworks asset, liability and cash effect from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The historical OE series contains apparent thousand-versus-million unit errors
audit_findings.magnitude: The supplied 2017 and 2019 OE figures are $5,626m and $6,798.2m, respectively—264 times and 319 times filed 2025 net income of $21.3m; exact corrections unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The observations enter the log-trend used to set the $11.0m OE anchor, which drives every forecast cash flow and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income increased 15%, or $2.7 million, to $21.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to $18.6 million for the same period in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The scale incompatibility is demonstrated: two observations are thousands of millions while the company's filed earnings and surrounding OE observations are measured in single or double-digit millions. The exact corrected figures remain unresolved because the underlying historical source units were not supplied. The too-hard flag does not prevent corrupted observations from affecting the computed anchor, so the current valuation cannot be relied upon.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild all annual OE observations from filed statements with source units shown, verify whether 2017 and 2019 should be $5.626m and $6.7982m, and rerun the anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Growth may require working-capital investment not captured in OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted incremental receivables, inventory and vendor-funding requirements would reduce forecast OE or increase the reinvestment charge supporting growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Our business requires working capital to operate and to finance accounts receivable and product inventory that are not financed by trade creditors.
audit_findings.explanation: The working-capital exposure is demonstrated, but its normalized valuation effect is not. June 2026 accounts receivable were $295.258m, while reported operating cash flow was strongly affected by receivable and payable timing. These figures establish substantial funding flows but do not establish the structural cash investment required for the 3% and 6% growth scenarios. If the forecast reinvestment charge omits that requirement, value is overstated.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile multi-year OE to operating cash flow and calculate normalized incremental accounts receivable plus inventory less operating vendor financing per dollar of growth; rerun each growth scenario with that reinvestment charge.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-derived earnings may be credited without acquisition reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: DSS total purchase consideration was $22.145m, 10.5% of the $210m base equity value; Data Solutions cost $15.9m at closing plus $2.2m of initial earn-out consideration; normalized annual acquisition reinvestment is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings enter historical OE and its trend, while acquisition payments and earn-outs occur outside ordinary operating OE and are not charged in the forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: Net sales and gross billings increased due to organic growth at our existing vendor lines and the full year impact of the DSS acquisition that closed in the third quarter of 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The numerator mismatch is demonstrated for historical results: FY2025 includes a full year of DSS earnings, and acquisitions are expressly part of the growth strategy, while the related purchase payments are investing or financing cash flows. Whether the forecast growth rates specifically require continued acquisitions remains unresolved, but the filed transaction amounts are large enough that omitting a normalized acquisition requirement is reasonably capable of materially overstating operating value.
audit_findings.action: Produce organic and acquired OE bridges for DSS and Data Solutions. Rerun growth using organic economics only, or deduct a normalized acquisition and earn-out cash requirement wherever acquired growth is retained.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may not be freely distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $56.563m cash add-back equals 26.9% of the $210m base equity value and $2.97 per diluted share; $18.8m of disclosed indefinitely reinvested foreign earnings equals 33.2% of that cash add-back and $0.99 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any restricted, locally required, tax-leaking or minimum operating cash should be excluded from the equity bridge or reduced for distribution costs.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has approximately $11.3 million of undistributed earnings in Canada and $5.3 million of undistributed earnings in the United Kingdom and $2.2 million of undistributed earnings in Ireland, which it continues to reinvest indefinitely, and therefore no withholding taxes related to its repatriation has been recorded.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds all June 2026 cash dollar-for-dollar. The filing demonstrates $18.8m of indefinitely reinvested foreign earnings, but undistributed earnings are not the same as foreign cash, so the inaccessible amount remains unresolved. Because the entire cash add-back is more than one-quarter of base equity value, its availability is material even though reducing it would reinforce, rather than reverse, the conclusion that value is below the $29.17 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain June 2026 cash balances by entity and jurisdiction, legal distribution restrictions, withholding-tax estimates and minimum operating-liquidity requirements; rerun the bridge using only net distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Contingent-consideration remeasurement may be a one-off retained in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed pre-tax remeasurement expense was $1.374m in 2025 and $3.618m in 2024; its inclusion in OE and after-tax valuation effect are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, noncash fair-value remeasurement reduces historical OE and can depress the trend anchor; actual earn-out cash payments instead belong in acquisition reinvestment when acquired growth is credited.
audit_findings.evidence: Contingent consideration is remeasured each reporting period using Level 3 inputs, and the change in fair value, including accretion for the passage of time, is recognized in acquisition related costs in the consolidated statement of earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The remeasurement amounts and their noncash accounting treatment are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether the annual OE bridges already normalized them. Their effect on the $11.0m anchor therefore remains an unresolved possibility. If retained, they understate normalized operating earning power, although removing them must not also remove the separate economic cost of actual acquisition payments.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every annual OE bridge for contingent-consideration remeasurement, remove any included after-tax noncash expense, separately retain actual earn-out cash in acquisition reinvestment, and rerun the trend and scenarios.
